rows.definition: CoverageReceipt (schema fak.debt-coverage-receipt.v1) is the machine-readable report BuildCoverageReceipt constructs from scanned debt lanes and findings, scoring discovery breadth over observed surface classes against detector depth over evaluated health dimensions.
rows.distinction: It audits how much of the repository surface space a debt-lane scan actually saw; it is not the serving-time SLO objective ReceiptCoverage, which measures the fraction of expected execution receipts collected.

rows.definition: ReceiptCoverage is the nativeperfslo Objective ("receipt_coverage") whose value is the fraction of expected execution receipts actually collected during a native-inference observation window, gated by MinReceiptCoverage (default 0.95).
rows.distinction: It is a runtime SLO metric over evidence collection while serving; it is not the static debtlane CoverageReceipt artifact that reports scan breadth and depth, and not the generic coverage fraction.

rows.definition: CPUModelParity is the *bool quality-evidence field (json cpu_model_parity) on Qwen38VulkanRawDecodeResult that the raw-decode bench sets when the Vulkan candidate's outputs match the CPU model reference across all runs.
rows.distinction: It is a per-trial pass/fail flag on one decode receipt; it is not a continuous similarity score such as CosineParity and not a generic parity comparison.

rows.definition: tools/cuda_abi_parity.py is the GPU-free static cross-check that reads the CUDA C-ABI seam (headers, cgo preambles, kernel definitions) as text and reports every prototype/definition/call-site mismatch before the remote nvcc link would catch it.
rows.distinction: It verifies that the header, preamble, and kernel source sets agree on one flat C ABI; it does not measure numerical agreement of results, and a clean run proves nothing about build success on a GPU node.

rows.definition: Disparity is the doc term used in notes and benchmark reports to name a measured gap between two quantities, e.g. the 4.20x-to-1.86x speedup gap resolved by the calibration fix in the MAC agentic 4x Qwen3.8 note.
rows.distinction: It names the size and direction of a gap between measurements; parity names the comparison itself and its match/lead/trail verdict, and a disparity claim does not imply a parity measurement exists.

rows.definition: internal/dogfoodcoverage (exposed as `fak dogfood-coverage`) is the stdlib-only Go port of tools/dogfood_coverage.py that evaluates fleet and journal dogfood KPIs into a coverage percentage with hard/soft gates and an A-F grade.
rows.distinction: It scores how much of the declared dogfood KPI space is evidenced across live journals; it is not test-statement coverage and not the generic coverage fraction.

rows.definition: DoseNumericParity ("numeric_parity") is the HIL micro-dose kind that runs a small device GEMV/GEMM and compares its numerics against the host reference to certify hardware compute correctness.
rows.distinction: It is one member of the closed HIL dose-kind vocabulary that probes hardware; it is not the acceptance-report NumericalParity pillar and not a benchmark parity report.

rows.definition: ErrEncodeUnsupported is the tokenizer sentinel returned when a tokenizer.json shape falls outside the leaf's encode gate, refusing offline text/id conversion for that tokenizer.
rows.distinction: It refuses encoding for unsupported tokenizer shapes; it says nothing about decode support, vocabulary coverage, or model maturity.

rows.definition: ErrNativeBeamSearchUnsupported is the agent sentinel wrapping every admission failure of bounded raw-logit CPU beam search: width and length-penalty bounds, an unmodified nonstreaming text request without tools or sampling modifiers, a plain dense CPU planner, and workspace reservation overflow.
rows.distinction: It is the typed in-process refusal for beam-search admission; the gateway wire code native_beam_search_unsupported is its HTTP projection, and neither claims general sampling support.

rows.definition: native_beam_search_unsupported is the closed HTTP error-code string the gateway writes with status 400 when native beam-search parameters fail validation or admission.
rows.distinction: It is the wire label clients see on refusal; ErrNativeBeamSearchUnsupported is the in-process sentinel it wraps, and the code identifies the refused capability rather than a missing provider protocol.

rows.definition: ErrNativeForwardCoverageInvalid is the model sentinel for incomplete, cardinality-mismatched, or otherwise malformed native forward-coverage evidence, including output-to-layer traversal mismatches and prefix-snapshot identity or geometry mismatches.
rows.distinction: It validates that forward-coverage evidence completely and consistently describes the executed layers; it does not judge whether the produced logits are correct.

rows.definition: ErrV41NativeUnsupported is the model sentinel for DeepSeek V4.1 native-path refusals, such as Engram look-ahead requiring an attached V4.1 model, explicit serial decode, and no speculative, DFlash2, or expert-parallel execution.
rows.distinction: It marks a specific V4.1 native execution path unavailable in this configuration; it is not the packed-tensor read refusal ErrV41PackedUnsupported.

rows.definition: ErrV41PackedUnsupported is the typed refusal for a V4.1 packed tensor read request the live shard cannot safely serve: an unadmitted config, unknown name, tensor outside the shard, dtype/shape disagreement with the inventory, a missing or malformed scale sibling, or a request over the caller's byte bound.
rows.distinction: It guards packed weight reads from live shards; it does not refuse native execution paths the way ErrV41NativeUnsupported does.

rows.definition: Config.HostCompletePrefixSnapshotSupported (fak#13338) reports whether the device-less HOST complete-prefix-snapshot route carries full v41ForwardSnapshot continuation state, admitting V4.1 planner prefix reuse without a device witness.
rows.distinction: It is the host-route eligibility predicate; the device route is InKernelBackendPrefixReuseSupportedFor, and both sit behind the bare-KV refusal rather than weakening it.

rows.definition: NumericalParity is the SubagentFanoutParity record (json numerical_parity) in the subagent fanout acceptance report: logit cosine similarity against a named reference GEMV with a minimum threshold and a passed flag, feeding Pillar 2.
rows.distinction: It is a recorded fidelity measurement with an explicit threshold; it is not a live comparison mechanism, not the Strix CosineParity score, and not a bare parity claim.

rows.definition: override_supported is the closed JSON meta key published on quarantined tool-result stubs by ctxmmu, ifc, and normgate stating whether the safety hold can be retrieved or overridden with a logged justification.
rows.distinction: It describes override availability for one safety hold; it is not generic feature support and it does not grant the override, which still requires a logged reason.

rows.definition: PARITY_MATCH is one of the three closed Strix ablation receipt verdicts (VERIFIED_LIFT | PARITY_MATCH | REGRESSION): the candidate arm stays within the speed and cosine-parity bounds of the baseline without a verified lift.
rows.distinction: It certifies equivalence within bounds; VERIFIED_LIFT additionally requires demonstrated lift, and a slow PARITY_MATCH is rejected by receipt validation.

rows.definition: Qwen38MTPBackendUnsupported ("backend_unsupported") is the Qwen38MTPDowngradeReason recorded when the backend is not ready for Qwen3.8 MTP speculative decoding, downgrading the session to ordinary decoding.
rows.distinction: It names the backend axis of the closed MTP downgrade vocabulary; model, precision, sampling, and depth failures carry their own members.

rows.definition: Qwen38MTPCorrectnessDiverged ("correctness_diverged") is the Qwen38MTPDowngradeReason recorded post-execution when the draft verifier's acceptance diverges from the reference trajectory, forcing a fallback decode.
rows.distinction: It is a post-execution correctness divergence; the pre-execution eligibility reasons (backend, model, sampling, depth) refuse before any draft work runs.

rows.definition: Qwen38MTPDepthUnsupported ("depth_unsupported") is the Qwen38MTPDowngradeReason recorded when the requested draft depth exceeds the supported maximum for Qwen3.8 MTP.
rows.distinction: It is the depth axis of the closed downgrade vocabulary; session-not-fresh, memory-unsafe, and policy-disabled states are separate closed reasons.

rows.definition: Qwen38MTPModelUnsupported ("model_or_artifact_unsupported") is the Qwen38MTPDowngradeReason recorded when the model or its artifact does not carry the MTP envelope required for Qwen3.8 speculative decoding.
rows.distinction: It is the model-axis reason; backend readiness, sampling mode, and depth each have their own closed members.

rows.definition: Qwen38MTPSamplingUnsupported ("sampling_mode_unsupported") is the Qwen38MTPDowngradeReason recorded when the request's sampling mode lies outside the greedy envelope MTP decoding admits.
rows.distinction: It is the sampling-mode axis of the same closed downgrade vocabulary; it is emitted alongside Qwen38SamplingDowngradeError details rather than replacing them.

rows.definition: rsi_maturity is the control-pane scorecard key (debt rsi_debt, script tools/rsi_maturity_scorecard.py) that reports RSI-maturity debt on the operator scoreboard debt page.
rows.distinction: It is one pane of the operator control plane aggregating RSI-maturity debt; it is not the generic maturity concept and not a per-capability maturity rung.

rows.definition: SupportsDeviceWeightDtype is the compute.Backend interface method reporting the exact dtype set the backend's MatMul has a resident case for, probed by the dense k-quant HAL staging seam and the MoE device gate/up seam.
rows.distinction: It is a per-backend dtype capability probe; SupportsHAL and SupportsHALKQuant are quant-format-level predicates at the model layer, not backend probes.

rows.definition: SupportsHAL is the QuantDescriptor method reporting whether that quant format is supported for device HAL weight staging.
rows.distinction: It is a per-format descriptor fact consulted when building HAL weights; SupportsHALKQuant is the model-layer predicate over k-quant kinds, and SupportsDeviceWeightDtype probes a concrete backend's MatMul dtypes.

rows.definition: SupportsHALKQuant(kind) is the internal/model package-level predicate reporting whether a k-quant kind has a HAL kernel somewhere, independent of any particular backend.
rows.distinction: It answers whether the model layer has a HAL kernel for the kind; the backend check (SupportsDeviceWeightDtype) separately answers whether this backend serves the dtype, and both must admit for device execution.

rows.definition: SupportsQ2K() bool is the optional q2kCapableBackend capability method advertising that a backend can matmul over packed Q2_K blocks without first expanding them to Q8/F32.
rows.distinction: It is the packed-Q2_K matmul capability asserted locally so serve wiring never names a concrete device backend; SupportsDeviceWeightDtype(Q2_K) only says the dtype has a MatMul case.

rows.definition: SupportsV41BF16Publish(rank) is the optional V41BF16PublishBackend contract method reporting whether the backend publishes BF16 rows for V4.1 on-device, probed at rank 1 by the op-coverage reader.
rows.distinction: It is one of the closed V4.1 op contracts the op-coverage reader classifies as device, host-fallback, or absent; absence routes the op to the host path rather than failing the request.

rows.definition: SupportsV41CompressorPool() is the optional V41CompressorPoolBackend contract method reporting whether the backend serves the V4.1 compressor-pool operation on-device.
rows.distinction: It is one of the closed V4.1 op contracts read by the single op-coverage reader; a false answer means host fallback for that op, not a refusal of the model.

rows.definition: SupportsV41EngramRowDecode() is the optional V41EngramRowDecodeBackend contract method reporting whether the backend decodes V4.1 Engram rows on-device.
rows.distinction: It is one of the closed V4.1 op contracts; the related encoding direction and the indexer-score contract are separate probes.

rows.definition: SupportsV41ExactRMSNorm(rows, tol) is the optional V41ExactRMSNormBackend contract method reporting whether the backend computes the V4.1 exact RMSNorm within tolerance on-device, probed at 4096 rows and 1e-6.
rows.distinction: It is one of the closed V4.1 op contracts with a numeric tolerance probe; approximate normalization paths do not satisfy it.

rows.definition: SupportsV41IndexerScore() is the optional V41IndexerScoreBackend contract method reporting whether the backend scores V4.1 indexer keys on-device.
rows.distinction: It is one of the closed V4.1 op contracts read by the op-coverage reader; it concerns indexer scoring, not Engram row decoding or MHC mixing.

rows.definition: SupportsV41MHC() is the optional V41MHCBackend contract method reporting whether the backend serves the V4.1 MHC stream operations (initial streams, split coefficients with Sinkhorn-normalized combinations, pre/post mixing) on-device.
rows.distinction: It is one of the closed V4.1 op contracts; absence permits caller selection of the host reference, and after selection an operation error propagates instead of replaying on CPU.

rows.definition: SupportsV41RoutedIDWeight(dt) is the V41RoutedIDBackend method reporting which weight dtypes the backend's V41MatVecID serves; CUDA and Vulkan admit Q2_K and Q3_K.
rows.distinction: It is the routed-ID matvec weight-dtype axis; the fused gate-up and down contracts are separate methods on the same interface.

rows.definition: SupportsV41TailRoPE() is the optional V41TailRoPEBackend contract method reporting whether the backend applies the V4.1 tail RoPE rotation to query/key tensors on-device.
rows.distinction: It is one of the closed V4.1 op contracts; the companion row and exact variants refine which rotation forms the backend serves.

rows.definition: unsupported_provider_protocol is the closed preflight refusal reason the fak ops run inference commands emit when the selected provider is not the admitted openai-compatible wire protocol.
rows.distinction: It is a CLI preflight refusal label written to the ops receipt; it is not a backend capability probe and it does not evaluate the model, only the provider protocol.

rows.definition: V41PhaseFieldCoverage is the struct type qualifying each legacy numeric V4.1 phase total with a status (measured, unavailable, not_applicable), reason, boundary, overlap, outcome, and measured/unavailable sample counts.
rows.distinction: It records how a phase number was obtained and how many samples back it; it is not the timing value itself, not a fault-attribution verdict, and not a forward-coverage completeness check.
